chapters.title: The Mind Is Not a Camera
chapters.tease: You are certain the car is in row C. It is in row F, and your brain painted the difference.

chapters.title: Two Speeds, One Driver
chapters.tease: A bat and ball cost one pound ten. If ten pence just arrived in your head, welcome to a very large club.

chapters.title: The Story Machine
chapters.tease: Your colleague does not reply. By evening you have a motive, a villain and a three-act drama. She was off sick.

chapters.title: Feelings Arrive First
chapters.tease: You know whether you like the house before the agent says deceptively spacious. The next forty minutes are just paperwork.

chapters.title: The Comfort of Certainty
chapters.tease: Sixty per cent chance of rain, no rain, app deleted. That is firing the bookmaker because the favourite lost.

chapters.title: Noise Pretending to Be Signal
chapters.tease: Sales up eleven per cent: pizza. Down nine: a louder speech. Nothing changed except the dice nobody mentioned.

chapters.title: The Tribe Votes Before You Do
chapters.tease: At a family dinner the table divides before anyone speaks. The vote was taken before the soup arrived.

chapters.title: Busy Is Not Thinking
chapters.tease: Thirty-one emails by eleven o'clock, and you feel productive in the way a hamster feels athletic.

chapters.title: Clever People, Silly Beliefs
chapters.tease: A double Nobel laureate swore by vitamin C. Sherlock Holmes's creator believed in fairy photographs. Clever is not immune.

chapters.title: The Fog Can Be Lifted
chapters.tease: Back in the car park, still thinking row C. This time you check the ticket, and that is the whole difference.

chapters.title: Define Your Terms
chapters.tease: Forty minutes into a meeting about whether the launch succeeded, both camps are right. They just mean different words.

chapters.title: Facts Versus Stories
chapters.tease: Your neighbour walks past without saying hello. By your front door you have a grudge, a motive and a speech.

chapters.title: Name the Real Problem
chapters.tease: The lifts were slow, so someone fitted mirrors. The complaints stopped, because the problem was never the lift.

chapters.title: Reason From Bedrock
chapters.tease: The builder says this is what kitchens cost. First principles says it is forty metres of chipboard, a sink and nine days.

chapters.title: Ask Why Five Times
chapters.tease: The barrier is broken because it is broken. Keep asking why, and you end up fixing a contract, not a person.

chapters.title: Invert, Always Invert
chapters.tease: Planning a wonderful holiday is hard. Planning a miserable one takes two minutes, and gives you a checklist.

chapters.title: Occam's Razor, Lightly Held
chapters.tease: The milk has gone. You do not investigate the fridge portal. You ask your son, who studies the ceiling.

chapters.title: Chesterton's Fence
chapters.tease: There is a pointless locked gate behind your house. Someone put it there, on purpose, with money.

chapters.title: Socrates Asks Again
chapters.tease: Your friend defines a good manager. You ask questions. By dessert the definition is much better and the wine has stopped coming.

chapters.title: The Map Is Not the Territory
chapters.tease: The app says eleven minutes. It does not mention the hill, the roadworks or the park that locks at dusk.

chapters.title: Confirmation, the Polite Liar
chapters.tease: Dan left at four one Tuesday. Since then you have noticed every early departure, and missed the night he stayed till nine.

chapters.title: The Anchor in the Room
chapters.tease: The agent mentions what next door sold for, then leaves you alone in the kitchen. You are not thinking about worktops.

chapters.title: Availability and the Evening News
chapters.tease: After the evening news you decide to drive to Lisbon instead of flying. You feel safer. You are not.

chapters.title: Hindsight Was Never Twenty-Twenty
chapters.tease: The project failed, and now everyone in the room saw it coming. Remarkably few of them wrote it down.

chapters.title: Sunk Costs and Sinking Ships
chapters.tease: The film has introduced a twin, the popcorn is gone, and you stay because the ticket cost fourteen pounds.

chapters.title: The Overconfident Expert
chapters.tease: The consultant is certain, in a large font. Two decades of checked predictions suggest the font is doing the work.

chapters.title: Survivors Write the Brochures
chapters.tease: The billionaire dropped out and bet the house. The others who did the same are at home, explaining to the bank.

chapters.title: The Halo and the Horns
chapters.tease: She is tall, articulate and wearing a very good jacket. By question three you have decided she is good with spreadsheets.

chapters.title: The Bias Blind Spot
chapters.tease: Eight chapters on bias, and you now see it everywhere. Except, curiously, in one particular person.

chapters.title: Steelman the Other Side
chapters.tease: You have the perfect rebuttal to your neighbour's road closure idea. It is aimed at a version she never said.

chapters.title: Second-Order Thinking
chapters.tease: You put up a bird feeder. By October you are running a buffet with a resident cat and pricing squirrel baffles at eleven at night.

chapters.title: The Circle of Competence
chapters.tease: You explain the housing market to a dinner table that includes a mortgage adviser. She lets you finish. That is the worst part.

chapters.title: Base Rates Before Stories
chapters.tease: Your friend's restaurant has a great chef and a story you can taste. A dull number at the back of your mind clears its throat.

chapters.title: Margin of Safety
chapters.tease: The app says forty minutes to the airport. The disappointing coffee at the gate is what a margin of safety tastes like.

chapters.title: Incentives Explain Most Things
chapters.tease: The sign above the sink begs you to wash your mugs. The sink is full of mugs. The sign is not the problem.

chapters.title: Opportunity Cost, the Invisible Bill
chapters.tease: You clear the garage on Saturday and nobody sends a bill. Something was still paid, without a receipt.

chapters.title: Feedback Loops
chapters.tease: The hotel shower has two settings, arctic and volcanic. You are not bad at showers. You are in a loop with a delay.

chapters.title: Thinking in Systems
chapters.tease: The third-floor printer jams every Monday. Everyone thinks it is temperamental, and that belief is load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Pareto Lens
chapters.tease: Forty-three unread emails and a scrolling to-do list. Your nagging sense that most of it does not matter has a name.

chapters.title: A Latticework, Not a Hammer
chapters.tease: To a man with a hammer, everything looks like a nail. Munger's fix was to carry a latticework instead.

chapters.title: Every Belief Is a Bet
chapters.tease: You are certain the barrier stays up till seven. Then a friend says want to bet a tenner, and certainty develops a draught.

chapters.title: Probability for Humans
chapters.tease: Thirty per cent chance of rain. Of the day? The town? The forecasters? People read that sentence every possible way.

chapters.title: Updating Like Bayes
chapters.tease: A positive test, ninety-five per cent accurate. It feels like ninety-five per cent odds. It is closer to one in fifty.

chapters.title: Calibration, the Quiet Virtue
chapters.tease: She says seventy per cent chance of rain, and it rains seven times in ten. Nobody writes songs about her.

chapters.title: Expected Value at the Kitchen Table
chapters.tease: The new washing machine costs four hundred pounds, and the assistant leans in, gentle as a priest, offering cover for ninety.

chapters.title: Fat Tails and Black Swans
chapters.tease: A turkey is fed for a thousand days, and grows more confident every morning. Then comes a Wednesday shortly before Christmas.

chapters.title: Luck Versus Skill
chapters.tease: Your nephew won the office sweepstake twice and now calls it a strategy. There is a simple test for that.

chapters.title: Regression to the Mean
chapters.tease: Worst sales week of the year. You are stern, you cancel the pizza, and sales recover. You have just been fooled.

chapters.title: Resulting: Judging the Dice
chapters.tease: A pass play, a yard from victory, intercepted. The worst call ever, said the headlines. Or just a bad bounce?

chapters.title: Ranges, Not Points
chapters.tease: Someone asks what the kitchen will cost and you say twenty thousand, like a postcode. You have seen no quotes.

chapters.title: What an Argument Actually Is
chapters.tease: Two people at a party have said the same thing four times, louder each time. That is not an argument. It is two weather reports.

chapters.title: Valid Is Not True
chapters.tease: All fish can fly. A salmon is a fish. So a salmon can fly. Flawless logic, and anyone who has met a salmon knows it.

chapters.title: The Usual Fallacies
chapters.tease: Learning the Latin names of fallacies is a pleasant hobby that makes you slightly worse company. Look at the animals instead.

chapters.title: Correlation Is Not a Confession
chapters.tease: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together every summer. Before you ban the ninety-nine, look at the sun.

chapters.title: The Burden of Proof
chapters.tease: Your neighbour says there is a ghost in his loft, and when you doubt it, says prove there isn't. You owe him nothing.

chapters.title: Extraordinary Claims
chapters.tease: In 2011 neutrinos seemed to beat the speed of light. The culprit turned out to be a loose cable.

chapters.title: Questions That Smuggle Answers
chapters.tease: Have you stopped cheating at Monopoly? Yes and no both lose. The question decided the case before you spoke.

chapters.title: Arguing to Learn, Not to Win
chapters.tease: Winning an argument makes you feel taller, and teaches you precisely nothing. There is a better way to lose.

chapters.title: Changing Your Mind in Public
chapters.tease: You said the new booking system would be a disaster. Three months on, the receptionist has started to hum.

chapters.title: The Charitable Reading
chapters.tease: I don't think the launch plan is realistic, says the email. In four seconds you decide she wants your job. She means the dates.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Door
chapters.tease: Forty minutes choosing between two greys called Elephant's Breath. Earlier, a three-year lease agreed over biscuits in the time it takes to boil a kettle.

chapters.title: The Pre-Mortem
chapters.tease: Declare the project dead a year early, and the quiet engineer will finally tell you how it died.

chapters.title: Satisficing Is Not Settling
chapters.tease: Three evenings, eleven tabs, a strong opinion on crumb trays, and still no toaster. You are eating cereal out of spite.

chapters.title: Regret Minimisation
chapters.tease: You have mentioned the idea at three Christmases, and your family have a special face for it. Ask the eighty-year-old you instead.

chapters.title: The Decision Journal
chapters.tease: You saw the last election coming. You always do. Your memory, a loyal and slightly corrupt employee, has been editing the files.

chapters.title: The Outside View
chapters.tease: Your friend's kitchen will be done in March. She has a spreadsheet and a builder called Dave. You ask how long kitchens usually take.

chapters.title: Options Over Plans
chapters.tease: You visited the coast once, on a bright June Saturday. The plan assumes February will be the same place.

chapters.title: Deciding Not to Decide
chapters.tease: Buridan's donkey starved between two identical bales of hay. Nobody has met him. Everybody has sat in the meeting.

chapters.title: Groups Without Groupthink
chapters.tease: Seven clever people agree unanimously, and everyone takes it as a good sign. The quiet one with the complaints file disagrees.

chapters.title: Good Decisions, Bad Outcomes
chapters.tease: You left three hours early and missed the flight. Your brother left forty minutes before and bought a sandwich. He will explain his method.

chapters.title: Attention Is the Raw Material
chapters.tease: You sit down to think about the Leeds job. Twenty minutes later you know whether otters hold hands. Leeds is slightly offended.

chapters.title: One Thing at a Time
chapters.tease: On a budget call with two other windows open, you feel like an octopus with a desk job. Then someone asks about the travel line.

chapters.title: Boredom Is a Workshop
chapters.tease: One window open, a man posting a canoe, and your phone at home. Around minute four, you finally get somewhere.

chapters.title: Sleep on It, Literally
chapters.tease: At eleven at night the Leeds question is enormous. At seven, over toast, the answer is obvious and slightly boring.

chapters.title: Thoughts at Walking Pace
chapters.tease: Forty minutes on one spreadsheet paragraph. You walk to the shop for milk, and by the second lamp post you have the answer.

chapters.title: Name It to Tame It
chapters.tease: Interesting choice. Let's discuss. You read it four times, feel something hot and vague, and say you are fine.

chapters.title: The Dichotomy of Control
chapters.tease: You check your email every eleven minutes, as if the chain of house buyers were visible from orbit. It moves nothing but your blood pressure.

chapters.title: The Gap Before the Reply
chapters.tease: The solicitor misspells your surname and asks for a document you sent twice. Your fingers start typing before your judgement finds its shoes.

chapters.title: Digital Fog
chapters.tease: Four minutes into the contract, your phone mentions a parcel, a stranger's work anniversary, a lonely game and some rain.

chapters.title: Deep Work, Shallow Water
chapters.tease: By Wednesday of the new job your calendar looks like Tetris played in a hurry, and the real work is wedged in the cracks.

chapters.title: Writing Shows You What You Think
chapters.tease: Your opinion about the office move felt solid for a fortnight, the way a cat does until you try to pick it up.

chapters.title: The One-Sentence Test
chapters.tease: Forty pages, plenty of charts, and when your manager asks what the report says by the lifts, out comes it's complicated.

chapters.title: Plain Words
chapters.tease: The strategy will leverage synergies to drive holistic value across the customer journey. Nobody can say what changes on Tuesday.

chapters.title: Outline Before You Opine
chapters.tease: You started writing paragraph one, and by paragraph six had written a moving tribute to the old supplier's delivery driver.

chapters.title: Explain It to a Twelve-Year-Old
chapters.tease: Your twelve-year-old niece asks what you do at work. Three questions later she has found the edge of your knowledge.

chapters.title: The Notebook Remembers
chapters.tease: In January you called it dead on arrival, twice. In June you find you always rather liked it.

chapters.title: Draw the Problem
chapters.tease: An hour of blame about late deliveries, then someone draws boxes and arrows, and the room goes quiet at the loop nobody had seen.

chapters.title: Edit Without Mercy
chapters.tease: Nine pages, and a sentence on page four rewritten six times. You admire it like a shed you built. It has to go.

chapters.title: Memos Over Slides
chapters.tease: Forty-two slides, four bullets each. Afterwards you recall the colour scheme and one joke. The decision fell between slides nineteen and twenty.

chapters.title: Teaching Is Learning Twice
chapters.tease: You built half the forecasting model and have used it weekly for three years. Teaching it to a graduate, you discover you never understood it.

chapters.title: Strong Opinions, Weakly Held
chapters.tease: People quote strong opinions, weakly held as permission to be loud. It was meant as a method, with an exit door.

chapters.title: Intellectual Humility
chapters.tease: Explain how a zip works, tooth by tooth. Watch your confidence drain out mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Scout, Not Soldier
chapters.tease: The soldier defends the position. The scout reports whether the bridge is intact, even when she hoped otherwise.

chapters.title: Curiosity as a Discipline
chapters.tease: By forty, many of us have quietly swapped curiosity for competence. Efficient, and slightly tragic. It can be learned back.

chapters.title: Thinking With Machines
chapters.tease: Your new colleague never sleeps, reads faster than a library, and is occasionally, cheerfully, completely wrong.

chapters.title: Disagreeing Well Together
chapters.tease: Five minutes in, the launch-date argument has become a contest about who is more reasonable. The date sits there like an unclaimed coat.

chapters.title: The Long Game of Judgement
chapters.tease: The senior nurse calls the doctor before the monitors complain. It looks like magic. It is mostly years of honest feedback.

chapters.title: Clarity Is Kindness
chapters.tease: Nine paragraphs, and the request to approve the budget by Friday is hiding in the seventh. You find it on Saturday.

chapters.title: Unbothered, Not Uninterested
chapters.tease: The server goes down at four on a Friday. One engineer panics, one has left, and one quietly opens the logs.

chapters.title: See Clearly, Then Act
chapters.tease: One plain sentence, owed by a book on clear thinking: clear thinking is a practice, not a talent.
